title: Chelow with tahdig
skill: Steamed rice with a crisp bottom

notes.1: One heavy 5-quart nonstick pot. The crust only forms evenly at this size.

move.title: Parboil, steam, and a golden crust
move.body: Chelow is Persian steamed rice: basmati parboiled in well-salted water, drained, then steamed so every grain stands apart. Tahdig, the bottom of the pot, is the prize: a golden crust formed over a layer of saffron yogurt rice. You'll parboil to the right bite, build the base, steam under a towel-wrapped lid, and turn the whole pot out onto a platter.

why.title: Rinse and soak
why.body: Rinsing removes surface starch; a 30-minute soak lets the grains absorb water, so they lengthen instead of breaking.

why.title: Parboil to al dente
why.body: Boiled in plenty of salted water until soft outside with a firm, white core, then drained. The rest of the cooking is steam.

why.title: The towel lid
why.body: A clean towel wrapped around the lid absorbs condensation, so water doesn't drip back and make the rice soggy. Tie its corners up over the handle, well away from the burner.

why.title: Heat for the crust
why.body: Medium-high heat for the first 10 minutes starts the crust; low heat for the next 40 lets it turn golden while the rice above steams.

wrong.fix: Set the pot base in cold water in the sink for 2 minutes; the steam loosens it. Use a nonstick pot next time.
It parboiled too long. Pull it while the core is still white.
Return it to medium heat for 5 minutes, checking the edge.

quiz.q: Why tie the towel's corners above the lid?
choices: So they can't reach the burner and catch fire
quiz.explain: It sits well away from the flame.

quiz.q: When do you drain the parboiled rice?
choices: Soft outside with a firm, white core
Saffron yogurt rice on a hot, oiled pot base

steps.text: Rinse the rice in the bowl, changing the water until it's nearly clear, then soak it in fresh water.
Crush the saffron and steep it in the hot water.
Bring the parboiling water and salt to a rolling boil in the stockpot. Drain the rice and add it.
Boil, stirring gently once or twice, until the grains are soft outside with a firm core.
Drain in the colander and rinse briefly with lukewarm water.

Mix 1½ cups of the rice with the yogurt and half the saffron water. Heat the oil and 1 tablespoon of the butter in the large pot (nonstick is best) and press the yogurt rice over the base in an even layer.
Spoon the rest of the rice over it in a mound. Poke 5 holes to the bottom with the spoon handle. Dot with the remaining butter and spoon over the rest of the saffron water.
Wrap the lid in the towel, tie the corners over the handle, and cover the pot tightly.
steps.tip: Keep the towel's corners well above the lid, away from the flame.

steps.text: Lower to the lowest heat and steam.
Lift an edge of the base with a thin spatula.

target.look: A deep golden crust, and fluffy separate grains above

steps.text: Set the pot in 1 inch of cold water in the sink for 1 minute. Cover with a large platter and, with oven mitts, invert in one motion.
steps.look: A golden, unbroken disk of crust on top.

steps.text: Cut the tahdig into wedges and serve with the chelow.
